items.informal_name: Injectivity of Geometric Sum Function for Finite Sets
items.type: ∀ {n : ℕ}, 2 ≤ n → Function.Injective fun s => ∑ i ∈ s, n ^ i
items.informal_description: For any natural number $n \geq 2$, the function mapping a finite set $s \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ to the sum $\sum_{i \in s} n^i$ is injective. This means distinct finite sets produce distinct geometric sums when evaluated at base $n$.

items.type:

  Function.Injective ↑NumberField.mixedEmbedding.fundamentalCone.expMapBasis
items.informal_description: The exponential map basis for the fundamental cone of a number field $ K $ is injective as a function from the real space of infinite places of $ K $ to itself.

items.informal_name: Injectivity of the Sum of Coefficients Times Exponentials in Akra-Bazzi Recurrence
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype α] {T : ℕ → ℝ} {g : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : α → ℝ} {r : α → ℕ → ℕ} [inst_1 : Nonempty α]
  (R : AkraBazziRecurrence T g a b r), Function.Injective fun p => ∑ i, a i * b i ^ p
items.informal_description: For an Akra-Bazzi recurrence with finite non-empty type $\alpha$, real-valued functions $a : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ and $b : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$, the function $p \mapsto \sum_{i \in \alpha} a(i) \cdot b(i)^p$ is injective on $\mathbb{R}$. This means that if $\sum a(i) \cdot b(i)^{p_1} = \sum a(i) \cdot b(i)^{p_2}$, then $p_1 = p_2$.

items.informal_name: Injectivity of Behrend's Map with Base d
items.type: ∀ {n d : ℕ}, Set.InjOn ⇑(Behrend.map d) {x | ∀ (i : Fin n), x i < d}
items.informal_description: The Behrend map with base $d$, which sends each function $x : \mathrm{Fin}(n) \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfying $x(i) < d$ for all $i$ to the natural number $\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} x(i) \cdot d^i$, is injective on this subset of functions.

items.type:

items.informal_description: The exponential map constructed as the product of scaled exponential homeomorphisms over all infinite places of a number field $ K $ is injective. items.informal_description: For any natural number $ a $ with $ a \geq 2 $, the function $ \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N} $ defined by $ n \mapsto a^n $ is injective.

items.informal_description: For any natural number $n \geq 2$, the function mapping a finite set $s \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ to the sum $\sum_{i \in s} n^i$ is injective. This means distinct finite sets produce distinct geometric sums when evaluated at base $n$.

items.informal_name: Injectivity of Digit Representation in Natural Numbers
items.type: ∀ (b : ℕ), Function.Injective b.digits
items.informal_description: For any natural number base $ b $, the function mapping a natural number $ n $ to its list of digits in base $ b $ is injective. That is, if two natural numbers have the same digit representation in base $ b $, then they must be equal.

items.informal_name: Injectivity of Behrend's Map with Base d
items.type: ∀ {n d : ℕ}, Set.InjOn ⇑(Behrend.map d) {x | ∀ (i : Fin n), x i < d}
items.informal_description: The Behrend map with base $d$, which sends each function $x : \mathrm{Fin}(n) \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfying $x(i) < d$ for all $i$ to the natural number $\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} x(i) \cdot d^i$, is injective on this subset of functions.

items.informal_name: Injectivity of Base-$ b $ Digit Conversion for Fixed-Length Lists with Digits Less Than $ b $
items.type: ∀ {b : ℕ}, 1 < b → ∀ (l : ℕ), Set.InjOn (Nat.ofDigits b) {L | L.length = l ∧ ∀ x ∈ L, x < b}
items.informal_description: For any integer $ b > 1 $ and natural number $ l $, the function that maps a list of digits (each less than $ b $) of length $ l $ to the natural number obtained by interpreting the list as digits in base $ b $ with the first element as the least significant digit is injective. That is, distinct such lists yield distinct numbers.

items.informal_name: Injectivity of the Inclusion of Good and Maximal Products into All Products
items.type:

items.informal_description: The function that maps the disjoint union of the set of good products and the set of maximal products containing a specific element into the set of all products over $ I $ is injective.

items.informal_name: Injectivity of Evaluation Map for Good Products
items.type:
∀ {I : Type u} (C : Set (I → Bool)) [inst : LinearOrder I],
  Function.Injective (Profinite.NobelingProof.GoodProducts.eval C)
items.informal_description: The evaluation function $\text{eval}_C$ that maps good products of elements in a linearly ordered set $I$—via component-wise conversion of Boolean values to integers (true $\mapsto 1$, false $\mapsto 0$) and multiplication—defines an injective function from the set of good products to the integers $\mathbb{Z}$. This means distinct good products have distinct integer evaluations under this construction.
